item.title: Nothing Exists Independently
item.description:
Another late night blog post after a very stressful day.

I guess the blog is now being used like my old one was again.

Something that scared me more today than what I was talking about yesterday: losing my laptop.

I thought it was about to go bad earlier because the keyboard was playing up, the trackpad was scrolling weirdly, and suddenly the whole thing was just a mess. This is exactly why I don’t let anyone else use it if I have the choice. Probably slightly irrational, but I know how I treat my things, and I know how other people treat theirs.

item.title: A Lot Left Unsaid
item.description:
It’s Tuesday the 29th of September, 10:35pm, and I sit in bed awake, staring at the ceiling.

Reminiscing on the past, looking into the future, but no further than a year or so away, thinking.

What do I know? What don’t I know? What should I know?

Usually, I start thinking like this after something big. Something catastrophic and life-changing that seems to change the fate of my future as I know it.

item.title: Another Month, Somehow
item.description:
Apparently I am doing this again.

I said in the last post that I would try not to disappear for another month, and then, rather impressively, I disappeared for another month. I don’t really know where September went. It feels like I wrote the last post about five minutes ago, and somehow we’re already at the end of the month again.

So, for the three people who actually read this thing, here’s what has been happening.

item.title: It Was Supposed to Be Simple
item.description:
Apparently I’ve been busy.

I say apparently because when I look back over the last month, I can’t quite work out where all of it went. There have been phones to fix, English assignments to submit at least three days later than I was supposed to, exams to study for, a new monitor to acquire, a computer to rebuild, and somewhere in the middle of all of that I decided that what my life really needed was a fifty cubic centimetre engineering problem with two wheels.

item.title: Five Dollars Well Spent
item.description:
I’ve been left unsupervised.

That’s probably the easiest explanation.

Some people go for long walks when they have a quiet week. Others finally watch the television they’ve been meaning to get around to for months. Apparently, I buy water-damaged MacBooks.

In my defence, it only cost five dollars.

I volunteer at a local recycling shop every Saturday, where all manner of interesting electronics eventually find their way through the door. This particular MacBook never even made it onto the shelf. It came with paperwork from Apple in Singapore explaining, in admirable detail, why it wasn’t worth repairing. The recommendation was straightforward enough: replace the logic board, replace several other assemblies while you’re at it, and move on.

item.title: Statistically Speaking...
item.description:
It’s mildly disconcerting, honestly.

Not dramatically so. She’s only away for ten days, and by the time she’s back I’ll probably have repaired something that shouldn’t have been repairable, broken something that was working perfectly happily beforehand, written another blog post, and somehow convinced myself that learning yet another obscure piece of technology is an excellent use of my time. Rationally, ten days is nothing.

Apparently my brain disagrees.

At precisely 9:58 this evening, my phone didn’t ring.

item.title: I've Seen This One Before
item.description:
It’s been a fairly boring week, which is unfortunate because those are significantly harder to write about.

School happened. Accounting happened. Physics happened. English happened. Another week quietly disappeared into the pile of weeks that came before it.

The interesting things all happened outside of school.

Last weekend disappeared almost entirely into the ThinkPad X1 Nano I’m writing this on now. What started as a laptop with no signs of life ended with me soldering wires directly onto a BIOS flash chip, reconstructing firmware images, and spending far too much time staring at hexadecimal data. By Sunday night it was working again. If you are slightly more technically inclined, you can read that one here

item.title: Seven Hundred Kilometres (or there abouts)
item.description:
I got back from Auckland yesterday.

Six hundred and fifty-eight kilometres away from Wellington, if we’re being precise, which turned out to be just far enough for my brain to start behaving differently. Or perhaps it was the eight and a half hours spent getting there.

By the time you’ve seen the ninety-eighth farm on the same road, eighty-five kilometres since the last turn and another hundred and five until the next, you’ve had time to think, to say the least. And think I did.

item.title: On Love
item.description: This was supposed to be a tech blog. Somewhere along the line it became something else, and I think we both know whose fault that is. I write these because she makes me, and she somehow enjoys reading my reflections on her, written about her, largely for her, in what I can only describe as an awkward third person that we’ve both just agreed to pretend is normal. So here we are again.

item.title: Overdue
item.description:
So much for posting every month. So much for “I’ll be updating this more.” Here we are anyway.

It has been barely over a week since the dawn of my 16th revolution of the sun, which feels like a reasonable excuse to finally sit down and write something. A lot has happened in a short amount of time, mostly involving computers going wrong and computers going right, which is on brand.

item.title: Last Sunday
item.description:
This one is late. Very late. But it’s worth writing down before it gets any further away.

Last Sunday I went out with her. Coffee shop, then wandering around the shops, then back to the coffee shop because apparently once wasn’t enough and I had absolutely no complaints about that. It was a good day. A genuinely, simply good day, which feels worth saying out loud because those aren’t always as common as they should be.

item.title: Slowly, Then All at Once
item.description:
She asked for a post and I had nothing. Which is a first, sort of. Usually there’s something rattling around worth writing about, but today it was just this vague sense that everything is moving both too slowly and too quickly at the same time, and I couldn’t work out how to make that into something worth reading. Then I realised that was exactly the thing worth writing about.

I remember when school felt like a drag. My earliest writing, the stuff from two or three laptops ago now, was full of it. It started on an old HP Elitebook, moved to the ThinkPad, then briefly lived on a Dell Latitude I picked up because it was small enough to actually carry to school without thinking about it. I gave the Latitude to my sister when I was done with it, which was the right thing to do, but the backups of everything I’d written went with it. She’s still using it, which is good. The ThinkPad is still sitting around despite being broken, which is less rational but I can’t quite bring myself to throw it out. Too much history in a thing that size.

item.title: Back On the Air
item.description:
Right. So. It’s been a while.

A few months of radio silence across basically everything. The blog, the socials, all of it. Life got in the way in the way it sometimes does and somewhere along the line I just stopped. Not intentionally, it just sort of happened. But I’m back, and I had a pretty packed weekend, so let’s get into it.

This weekend has been a funny mix of making money and spending it. About a year ago I started making 3D printed morse keys as a little side hustle. Nothing serious, just a way to scrape a bit of cash from the hobby. They were the first thing I ever sold, ever, and there’s something strange and good about making actual money from something you built with your hands. I kept at it for a while then drifted off, as I tend to do. Then out of nowhere this weekend three orders landed at once. Not life changing stuff, about $50 all up, but that’s not really the point. It got me back in the mood for it and that’s worth something on its own.

item.title: Server testing
item.description: Nothing thrilling at all with this one, but if it’s visible after 5:40pm on 23/11/25 NZST then I have successfully implemented a much more automated workflow. This means I can write as much as I want, and literally push one button which runs a .bat script that pushes it to Github after prompting me only for a commit message. My server then has another script which hopefully runs every 20 minutes past the hour (3 times an hour, at :00, :20, and :40) if I wrote it correctly that should delete the old directory and automagically pull the updated copy from Github.
